transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I hope I explain this right. It's probably nothing major, maybe I'm just a little overtired from work, but... I've been having a hard time keeping my words in a straight line lately. 

Like, I'm an orderly, and I'll start talking to one of the nurses about an overnight shift, but then my brain just sort of... jumps? And suddenly I'm talking about soccer, or, um, paint colors, and then jumping to patient charts. It's really embarrassing, honestly, because I can see everyone getting lost when I talk, and I hate making things confusing for them. I really try hard to be clear, I promise. 

Is... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Aside from these communication difficulties, have you noticed any recent periods where you felt unusually energetic, had a decreased need for sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't feel unusually energetic. If anything, I'm just regular tired, you know? Like I said, work has been pretty busy. 

I sleep okay, I think. I try to get my full eight hours so I can be at my best for the patients and the nurses. I know how important it is to be rested. And my thoughts... well, they jump around like I mentioned, but they don't feel like they're racing or going super fast. Just... getting a little jumbled sometimes. 

I hope that makes sense? I really haven't had anything like what you're describing, I don't think. Is it okay that I don't have those symptoms?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't hear or see?

Oh, um... no. No, I definitely haven't had anything like that. 

Working on the floor as an orderly, you know, I see a lot of patients who do struggle with hearing voices or seeing things, and I always try to be really patient and gentle with them. But I promise I don't have anything like that going on myself. My mind plays tricks on me with the words sometimes, like I said, but there aren't any voices or... or visions or anything scary like that. 

I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. I just want to be completely honest with you so I don't mess up your evaluation. Am I doing okay with answering your questions so far? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you frequently struggle with staying focused on tasks, sitting still, or acting without thinking things through?

Um... no, not that I can remember. I mean, school was... school, you know? I wasn't always the top of the class or anything, but I tried really hard to be a good student and not cause any trouble for the teachers. 

I definitely didn't run around or act out. I always wanted to make sure I was following the rules and doing what I was supposed to do. Sometimes I might have daydreamed a little, just like any kid, but I don't think I had any real trouble focusing or sitting still. I always tried to be respectful. 

Is that... does that help? I hope I'm not leaving anything important out. I just want to give you the right information.
Do you find that you feel mentally exhausted or physically drained after you have to concentrate on tasks at work?

Um, well, I guess work can be a little tiring sometimes, just because it's a busy floor, you know? But I wouldn't say I feel totally drained or exhausted from concentrating. 

I really try my best to stay sharp and do a good job for the nurses. Sometimes if I have to focus really hard on getting a room set up perfectly or double-checking the supply lists, I might feel a little... just normally tired afterward? Like anyone would after working hard. But I always make sure I have enough energy to finish my shift and do what's asked of me. 

I don't want it to sound like I can't handle my job or anything. I really love working there. Do you think it's normal to just feel regular tired after a long shift? I hope that's an okay answer.
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your day worrying about many different things, such as your job, your health, or your finances, in a way that feels hard to control?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I worry a little bit, sure, just like... like making sure I pay my rent on time or hoping I'm doing a good enough job at work. But it's nothing out of control. 

I definitely don't spend all day worrying. I try to stay really positive and focus on helping the patients. If I get a little stressed, I just take a deep breath and keep working hard. I wouldn't want my supervisor to think I'm too anxious to do my job, because I really can handle it, I promise. 

I'm just a normal amount of careful about things, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you ever had a head injury, a seizure, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions that affect your brain or nervous system?

Um, no... no, I haven't. I've never had a seizure or hit my head hard or anything like that. I've always been really lucky to be pretty healthy physically. 

I try to be super careful, especially at the hospital, you know? I always follow the safety rules when I'm moving equipment or helping out on the floor, so I've never gotten hurt. I definitely wouldn't want a physical problem to keep me from being reliable at work. 

So, no, nothing wrong with my nervous system or anything. I hope that's helpful? I'm just trying to make sure I give you exactly what you need to know.
When you feel like your words are getting jumbled or your thoughts are jumping, do you notice yourself feeling an intense sense of mental fatigue or a feeling of 'brain fog' at those exact moments?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, when my thoughts get a little messy like that, it's not so much a heavy fog, really. I just... sometimes I have a little trouble focusing? 

Like, I'll be looking at a patient note, or maybe just a bill at home, and I might read the same page two or three times, and... I just don't quite catch what it says right away. Or if I'm at the grocery store trying to pick something out, I can get a little stuck, you know? Just frozen for a second trying to decide. 

But I always figure it out eventually! I don't want it to sound like I'm too confused to do my job or take care of myself. It's just a little blip sometimes, and I'm sure everybody gets that way when they're trying to be really careful, right? I try really hard to double-check everything so I don't make mistakes. Is it okay that I get a little stuck sometimes? I hope that doesn't mean I'm doing a bad job.
Do you often find yourself feeling down, sad, or like you have lost interest in the things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I guess everyone has their off days, right? I mean, I try really hard to keep a smile on for the patients, because they need it, but... lately, I guess it's been a little harder. 

I don't want you to think I'm not grateful for my job or anything, because I am! It's just... most days, from the minute I wake up, I just feel this... this really heavy, empty feeling. It's hard to explain without sounding like I'm complaining, which I promise I'm not trying to do. 

But, um... sometimes, after my shift is over, I'll just sit out in my car in the parking lot. And... I end up crying for a while before I can even start the engine to go home. I don't let anyone at work see me like that, though! I always make sure I'm out of the building first. 

I just... I want to do a good job, and I hope feeling this way doesn't mean I'm failing. Do you think it's normal to feel that heavy sometimes when you work in a hospital? I just want to make sure I'm handling things the right way.
Have you felt this heavy, empty feeling and experienced these 'blips' in your thinking at any other time in your life, or is this something completely new that only started recently?

Um... well, it's not exactly new, no. I mean, I hope it's okay to admit this, but... it's been happening for a while now. Maybe about... a year and five months? Give or take? 

I really tried to just push through it, you know? Because I wanted to show my supervisors that I was flexible and a team player. It all kind of started when they changed my schedule. I used to be on steady day shifts, which was great, but then they needed people for rotating nights and... and some overtime. And of course, I said yes, because I wanted to help out the unit! 

But, um... ever since then, my sleep got all turned around, and that's when the heavy feeling and those little focus blips kind of started creeping in. I really hope you don't think I'm blaming the job, though! I'm so lucky to have it. I just... I think my body is still trying to adjust, maybe? Is it normal for a schedule change to throw someone off for that long? I'm just trying to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
